research.summary: Appointed Republican Sen. Jon Husted is defending the seat JD Vance vacated against former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown, in a race Axios calls a toss up that could decide Senate control. With more than 400 million dollars spent or reserved and no debates planned, the contest centers on costs, data centers and Husted's record, while Republicans press cultural attacks on Brown.

issues.why: Brown says lowering costs is his top priority and accuses Husted of voting to raise prices, while Husted pitches tax credits and job training so Ohioans earn more.
Brown calls Husted the face of data centers in Ohio, and Husted introduced a bill on data centers covering their power costs that Democrats blocked.
Brown says ending the war would be his first priority, while Husted wants it to end on terms favorable to America.
Brown ties Husted to FirstEnergy and drug companies, calling him special interest Jon.
Republican ads accuse Brown of supporting gender transition care for minors, an attack also used in his 2024 loss.

storylines.title: Obama rallies with Brown in Cleveland
storylines.what: Former President Obama campaigned with Brown and Acton, joking that Husted and Ramaswamy act like they never heard of Trump. Brown named Musk, Thiel and Trump as billionaires backing Husted.

storylines.title: Husted distances himself from Ramaswamy ad
storylines.what: Husted told the AP he would not have run the governor nominee's ad featuring Amy Acton's estranged mother, as Ohio Republicans worried about fallout with women voters.

storylines.title: No debates planned
storylines.what: Axios reports no debates are planned between Husted and Brown before Election Day.

storylines.title: Ad attacking Brown on gender care
storylines.what: An attack ad circulating against Brown accuses him of supporting gender transition for youth. Brown's campaign says the focus distracts from economic issues.

storylines.title: Brown's High Cost Husted Tour
storylines.what: Brown has held High Cost Husted events tying Husted to rising prices, while Husted says Brown has few signature achievements after 32 years in Congress.

storylines.title: GOP surges resources into Ohio
storylines.what: About 250 million dollars was spent on Ohio ads by the end of September with Republicans generally ahead, and AFP Action says it knocked more than 700,000 doors for Husted.

storylines.title: Trump and Vance rally for Husted
storylines.what: Trump and Vance made three combined rally visits to Ohio by mid October to boost Husted, who said he felt a shift in energy.

events.title: Data center power costs
events.prompt: Ohio families are seeing higher electric bills as data centers multiply, and your opponent says you are on the wrong side. You must lay out a data center position.

opts.label: Make them pay full cost
opts.say: Require data centers to pay the full cost of their electricity so residents are not stuck with the bill.

opts.label: Voluntary cost sharing
opts.say: Ask states to consider having data centers cover power costs while keeping the investment coming.

opts.label: Build more power
opts.say: Cut regulation on nuclear, gas and pipelines so supply grows and prices fall.

events.title: Ramaswamy ad fallout
events.prompt: Your party's governor nominee is running an ad featuring his opponent's estranged mother and reporters want your reaction.

opts.label: Condemn it loudly
opts.say: Call the ad despicable and say it shows who the other side really is.

opts.label: Would not run it
opts.say: Say you would not have run that ad and pivot back to costs.

opts.label: Defend free speech
opts.say: Say voters can judge the ad and the media should focus on the other party.

events.title: Iran war and fuel prices
events.prompt: Diesel is at record highs and voters link it to the war with Iran. You are asked what you would do first in the Senate.

opts.label: End the war now
opts.say: Make ending the war the first order of business to bring fuel prices down.

opts.label: End it on good terms
opts.say: Push for a quick end on terms favorable to America while protecting troops.

opts.label: Back the president
opts.say: Support the administration's strategy and blame past weakness for the conflict.

events.title: Answering the culture ad
events.prompt: A heavy ad buy accuses one candidate of backing gender transition care for minors, the same attack used in 2024.

opts.label: Call it a distraction
opts.say: Say the attack distracts from prices and special interests and stay on the economy.

opts.label: State a middle line
opts.say: Say parents and doctors should decide with clear limits for minors.

opts.label: Press the attack
opts.say: Keep hammering the issue as proof the opponent is out of step with Ohio.
